Boogle rail map

The whole network at true plan position, from the data the game and the blockout read (generated by dev/level/rail-map.ts). World metres, north up. Every corridor is double track on 4 m centres, left-hand running (the up track, away from Home, on the left); at this scale the two tracks are spread apart so both stay visible, and come back to their true 4 m when you zoom in. Plan: docs/plans/rail-map.md.

Home has one terminus, the owner's pick (9 November): both lines at buffer stops beside one island, the table on its own engine spur.

18track ends, today and planned

Lines

Length along the drawn centreline. Trains: the plans' counts; for tentative lines an estimate from generic-lines' wait bound (no wait for a train your way over about a minute: round trip × 1.26 / 60 s). Each end as planned, then → as proposed. End to end: every halt a stop, 5 s dwell, 3.5 m/s² at both speeds (the engine-garage brief's comparison: engines and cars are bought per line). A line is flagged when the longer boiler saves under 10 s end to end non-stop (trains stop on request); one non-stop leg needs about 1143 m for that.

Every track end

The owner's rule (10 November): a track that ends has buffers and is marked a terminal; otherwise it runs through or loops. Before: 3 buffers, 4 stub, 8 crossover, 3 loop. After: 9 terminal, 3 buffers, 3 temporary, 2 loop, 1 through.

WhereBuildToday / as plannedCompliesProposedCost
Line 1, Village (Home: road 1's buffers, s -5.53)livebuffers: Home (the owner's pick, 9 November): road 1 runs straight at bearing 70° along the island (deck s 2.8-20.8) to buffer stops at s -5.53, abeam of road 2's; its last 2.9 m beside the forge's south wall is the forge's goods dock.yesterminal: Buffers, the Village end board and the concourse 1 m behind them: Home is both lines' terminus. Line trains never reach the table (it is on the engine spur).Home-station step 9 (buffer stops and dressing, look only).
Line 2, Village (Home: road 2's buffers, s -2.6)livebuffers: Home: road 2 runs along the island's other edge (deck s 5.7-23.7) to buffer stops at s -2.6. The engine spur leaves it at s 5.5 to the right for the 9.6 m table; the cart's leg joins it at s 26.yesterminal: Buffers and an end board, as line 1's. The cart stops at these buffers beside the forge rack (home-station's ruling 3).Home-station step 9 (look only), after the flip.
The Roundhouse's open stall (Home: the table's 190° road)livestub: Home: the engine spur (R 15, 60°) to the table, and three radial stall roads at 160°, 190°, 220° (the 190° one open, the others ruin outlines), each 9 m deep. No buffer stop at the stall's back.nobuffers: Buffers at the open stall's back wall; the shed is the terminal marking. Line 1, Camp (rail end s 221)livestub: Single terminal track from the s 182 stub turnout past the Camp platform (s 195-219) to a bare rail end at s 221. The ridge falls 32.5 m beyond (generic-lines Level findings).noterminal: Buffers at s 220 and an end board; the platform reads as a terminus. No loop: the ridge falls 32.5 m, so the camp is truly the end of line 1. Behind: the timber camp and the drop.View only.
Line 2, Far Head while it is the end (before Q6)v26crossover: A facing crossover at s 490-512 turns up trains onto the down track short of Far Head (stop 524); the up track runs on past it to the laying frontier, and Far Head's up platform waits, chained.partlytemporary: Keep the crossover (a temporary turnback for the first hour); the laid rails' end at the Q6 frontier gets the track layer's own buffer beam and a 'line under construction' board.View only. Long trains: Far Head stop from s 524 to 526, so the tail clears the crossover (v26 catalog).
The laying frontier (each stretch while it is laid)livestub: Wherever the machine has stopped, the rails end with the track layer parked on them.partlytemporary: The machine is the buffer: a buffer beam on its back end and a board, so the end of the laid line reads as 'being built'.View only.
Line 2, the pier head (rail end s 743; Q6 to v27)livestub: One terminal track from the s 556 stub turnout down the pier to a bare end 24.3 m over the sea, the track layer parked on it (its loco back at s 734.4).notemporary: Buffers at s 742.5 with a Pier end board, lifted by the machine when Q7 lays on (v27). Behind: the bents and the raised leaf.View only (v27 removes them). Long trains with the longer engine: pier stop from s 726.5 to 725.
Line 2, the moving railhead over bents 7-13 (v27, before the Meet)v27buffers: A stub end with a buffer stop (RING_RAILHEAD_KIT), the railhead platform, lever, rack and jib, moving 20 m per bent; the stub merges 20 m short.yesbuffers: As planned, plus an end board on the buffer. A longer-engine train stops 2 m shorter (its nose would reach the buffer face).v27 data (the end stop for long trains).
Ring Island halt while it is the end (v27)v27loop: R1's balloon loop, r 40 m, centred 48 m east of the halt; as laid out its neck runs 12 m on and then 30.6 m back south to the circle (a 165° reversal, then a 12° kink onto the circle): it can't be run as drawn.partlybuffers: Recommended (owner question 2): both tracks run on 15 m past the platforms to buffers and an end board at u 483, facing the way the line will go on; a facing crossover on the Way before the halt (about u 395-417), as Far Head's; trains stand at the east platform (the works side); the west lever is chained and plaqued with the branch. No train is ever turned. The alternative, a turning loop, is undrawn: a circle wholly east of both tracks can't take the up (west) track without crossing the down track, so it needs a merge to one track first or a teardrop about 80 m wide astride the line, and it cuts up to 12 m into the cone.A small R1 amendment (the crossover and buffer positions; RING_LOOP out of line 2's row); R2b drops the loop deck; R3a loses its loop leg. Then through when line 2 itself runs on.
Line 2 to High Gorge, High Gorgev27crossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside High Gorge; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: Line 2 runs on through the Ring Island halt along the west shore (no Ring top, ruling 3) and ends in the High Gorge split: buffers and a crossover before them, the White Wall's last span arriving beside it as a second platform.The branch's bump: line 2's row grows (like `extends: 1`); the catalog (src/sim/railway-world-lines.ts) already draws it.
North-south line, High Gorgelatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside High Gorge; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: A terminal at High Gorge's low station (3 m in the split), beside line 2's platform.Map data.
North-south line, Original Islandlaterloop: A 40 m turning loop past Original Island.yesloop: The incline and the causeway are one north-south line through Bell Rock (they are collinear), at the water: it goes on to a sunken causeway, so it never needs height. Kept: The Boogler's island is the ending; the train circles it.Map data and the hub's station plan; Bell Rock on two levels, the bay line on the skerry at 15 m above it (owner question 3).
Bay line, West landinglatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside West landing; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: A bay platform at the one West landing station (ruling 6), buffers against the town's shore wall: Home is where lines end, on foot between.Map data.
Bay line, Lantern Notchlaterloop: A 40 m turning loop past Lantern Notch.yesloop: Canopy keeps its loop while it is the end (stages 3/5-8); at stage 8 the bay line runs on to Lantern Notch, where the loop stays (the arch is the end of the world).Stage 8's bump.
Bay trestle, Ring Island haltlatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside Ring Island halt; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: Canopy-first only: a terminal with buffers at the island halt's west side. Not a shuttle: it runs on through Bell Rock to Canopy Town as one line (the review's finding 6), so the first trip to the new town needs no change of train.Map data.
Bay trestle, Bell Rocklatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside Bell Rock; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.nothrough: Canopy first: through Bell Rock (on the skerry, at 15 m, the bay line's level) onto the cleft to Canopy Town. The bay shortcut arrives at stage 4 as the second line into Bell Rock, a terminal there.Map data.
Cave line and the White Wall, West landinglatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside West landing; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: The ring's Home end: buffers at the West landing station, beside the bay line's platform; the walk to the Village halts is the hub (ruling 6).Map data.
Cave line and the White Wall, High Gorgelatercrossover: A scissors crossover 35 m inside High Gorge; its two tracks still end past the platforms, unmarked.noterminal: The row runs through Port Quay (High Port is the crane) and on as the White Wall to High Gorge, where it ends beside line 2 as a second platform (the greybox route, ruling 2; no lap). Stages 6-7: buffers at the quay while the Wall is unbuilt, the crane behind them.Map data (the lift leg leaves the rail catalog).

Services, for both branch orders

The proposals' services (the ring as one line, each line's ends as proposed), drawn on the map with the "Services" buttons. Grey legs aren't built in that order or were removed by a ruling: lift, the cave line's climb to High Port: the crane lifts instead (the rulings' knock-on). The blockout catalog (src/sim/railway-world-lines.ts) was regenerated for the greybox route's step 1: it has no lift leg and no Ring top halt, and its line 2 extension ends at the Ring Island halt (R1's data supersedes that draft).

High Gorge first

  • Line 1: Village to Camp: two terminals.
  • The ring (line 2 grown): Village, Quarry, Far Head, the pier (homeward only), the Meet's halt, Ring Island (v27), High Gorge (stage 3), Canopy Town and Port Quay (stage 7, the White Wall line), Saltpan, West landing (stage 6: the cave line, its own row with its own trains until stage 7 joins the halves). Both ends at Home, a walk apart.
  • Bay line: West landing, Bell Rock on the skerry (stage 4), Canopy Town (stage 5), on to Lantern Notch (stage 8).
  • North-south line: High Gorge's low station, Bell Rock at the water (stage 4), the Original Island (stage 8).

Canopy Town first

  • Line 1: Village to Camp: two terminals.
  • The ring (line 2 grown): As Gorge first, but line 2 runs on from Ring Island to High Gorge at stage 5.
  • Island to Canopy line: Stage 3: Ring Island (a terminal at the halt's west side), the bay trestle to Bell Rock (on the skerry), the cleft to Canopy Town: one line, so the first trip to the new town needs no change of train. On to Lantern Notch at stage 8.
  • Bay line (the shortcut): Stage 4: West landing to Bell Rock, the second line into Bell Rock, a terminal there (walk-between).
  • North-south line: Stage 5: High Gorge's low station, Bell Rock at the water; the Original Island at stage 8.

Keep clear at Home: the grown Roundhouse

The table grows from 9.6 m to about 16 m, with 16 m stalls, as an upgrade (the engine-garage brief), and only ever at Home. Kept clear: a sector from 130° to 250° (clockwise from north), r 26 m, south of Home's table on its spur, plus the grown table (r 8 m); nothing in town moves. The engine-garage brief's "30 m on the stall side" and this become one footprint. Within 26 m of the table:

Cargo loaders

Loaders stand Home-side of the passenger car's mark in both directions: today's trains are push-pull (train-view.ts poses the engine at +s), and with buffers at Ring Island no train is ever turned. docs/brainstorms/station-deposit.md's review puts each yard at the foot of the down platform's back ramp, mid-platform, on the premise that each direction's cargo cars trail at opposite ends. The two agree on the side of the track (the down platform's, the Works side at the Quarry) and differ along it by 4-11 m; the yard's premise holds only where a line turns its trains on a loop (stage 8's two loops). Build 1's yards stay where they are; build 2's gantry has to reach from the back ramp's foot to the cargo cars, across the deck's end ramp, which neither brief has drawn.

  • Split-rock Works rack (footings, the kiln): s 178.9, 12.8 m right of line 2's track, 8.9 m pier-side of Quarry's mark (s 170). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 166.3 to 158.9 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the down (right) side.
  • The kiln: s 189.9, 64.2 m right of line 2's track, 19.9 m pier-side of Quarry's mark (s 170). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 166.3 to 158.9 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the down (right) side.
  • The pier rack: s 733.4, 3.5 m right of line 2's track, 8.4 m pier-side of Pier's mark (s 725). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 721.3 to 713.9 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the down (right) side.
  • The forge rack (rails; Home, on the island's apron by the buffers): s -1.1, 2.7 m left of line 2's track, 19.4 m Home-side of Village, line 2's mark (s 18.25). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 14.6 to 7.2 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the up (left) side. The rack stands on the island's apron between the buffers and the deck's head ramp, 6.6 m behind the last cargo car: the cargo end, on the island, so rails go from rack to car without crossing a track. The recovery rack (the Village yard) stands at 905, 1.
  • The Roundhouse's open stall (Home): s 12.9, 28.2 m right of line 2's track, 5.4 m Home-side of Village, line 2's mark (s 18.25). Not a loader: the shunter brings stock from the stall over the table and up the spur, which leaves road 2 at s 5.5.
  • The depot (line 2's camp, the cart): s 184.4, 18.8 m right of line 2's track, 14.4 m pier-side of Quarry's mark (s 170). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 166.3 to 158.9 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the down (right) side.
  • Line 1's timber camp (logs): s 182.5, 5.8 m right of line 1's track, 22.8 m Home-side of Camp's mark (s 205.3). A loader serving a standing train sits at the cargo cars: s 201.6 to 194.2 (cars 2-4, Home-side of the passenger car in both directions: push-pull, never turned), on the down (right) side.

With buffers the train is never turned, so the cargo cars are Home-side of the mark as everywhere else: the loader at u 436.9 to 444.3 m, east of the platform's south half.
